---
title: "Welcome to the 11.118/218"
format: html
---

::: page-container
Urban science draws on statistics, visualization, and spatial analysis techniques to gain deeper insights into cities and actively contribute to their development.

In this course, we’ll dive into the dynamic world of urban science by learning how to tell stories about cities and neighborhoods, covering a range of topics including demographic analysis, environment and transportation, and using R as our primary quantitative analysis and interactive visualization tool.
:::

## Schedule

```{r}
#| echo: false
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)

schedule <- data.frame(
  Week = seq(1, 14, 1),
  Topic = c(
    "Contextualize Data Science for Cities",
    "Statistical Descriptions of Data",
    "Visual Descriptions of Data",
    "Sourcing and Working with Spatial Data",
    "Census Data",
    "Interactive Mapping and Data Visualization",
    "Web Apps; Midterm Exam",
    "Statistical Modeling and Interpretation",
    "Predictive Modeling and Supervised Learning",
    "Data Challenges, Missing Data Imputation",
    "Classification Models",
    "Unsupervised Learning and Clustering",
    "AI in Planning; Project Work",
    "Presentation"
  )
)

schedule |>
  kable(
    format = "html",
    col.names = c("Week", "Topic"),
    align = c("c", "c")
  ) |>
  kable_styling(
    bootstrap_options = c("bordered", "striped", "hover", "condensed"),
    full_width = FALSE
  ) |>
  column_spec(1, width = "2em") |>
  column_spec(2, width = "20em") |>
  pack_rows(
    "Module 1: Descriptive Data Science", 1, 7,
    label_row_css = "background-color: #f2f2f2; text-align: left;"
  ) |>
  pack_rows(
    "Module 2: Predictive and Statistical Modeling", 8, 14,
    label_row_css = "background-color: #f2f2f2; text-align: left;"
  )
```
